products.title: Terroir Culture by Ratnagiri Estate
products.body_html:
Terroir, the unique mix of a place’s soil, climate, elevation, and even its flora and fauna, influences how a coffee grows and tastes. At Ratnagiri, that sense of place goes a step further. The team harnesses microbes from the surface of coffee cherries grown at the estate and develops them into ‘terroir’ cultures in an in-house lab. To bring this special coffee to life, one such culture was put to work. 

Ripe cherries for this lot came from the estate's Godown Patte block, where coffee grows at 1,341 MASL. While picking, brix readings complemented honed instinct. At the sorting stage, both density and colour determined which cherries advanced. Next, an ozonator removed surface microbes before cherries moved to bio-fermenters. This step, a hallmark of Ratnagiri's processing, cleared the way for controlled fermentation. Next, the terroir culture and lactic acid bacteria steered a 48-hour, CO₂-rich ferment. And finally, after 29 days of slow drying, the coffee was ready for milling. 

What entered our roasteries had us all excited. Roasted to a light profile, it brews rose-perfumed cups with rich floral and fruity layers. During cupping, it reminded us of rose, lychee, custard apple, and forest honey. In the finish, the coffee’s floral character stood out again, with a rose tea-like note.  

To take in its complexity, we recommend enjoying this coffee black. You can't go wrong when you brew it as a pour over or using an AeroPress.

Recommended Resting Period: 9 days

products.title: Kolli Berri Estate
products.body_html:
This medium-dark roast, nurtured in a completely women-run farm, brews cups with a chocolatey and nutty flavour profile. It hails from the beautiful Kolli Berri Estate, set in Chikmagalur, Karnataka.

products.title: Baarbara Estate - Whiskey Barrel Aged
products.body_html:
This coffee’s journey began at Baarbara Estate in the foothills of Baba Budangiri, the origin of coffee in India. It was shaped by a process the estate has spent years refining, with one precise outcome in mind: a cup where whiskey’s character and coffee’s identity sit in balance. 

The barrels this coffee was aged in were brought in within 15 days of malt being removed. They were then housed in a covered, controlled space, away from direct sunlight and changing weather. The coffee beans were allowed to rest in them for nearly four months, with the barrels carefully turned every few days, and the beans cupped regularly as the flavours evolved. Over time, the coffee gently absorbed the oak’s character while holding on to its own. 

The result is a medium roast with notes of red plum, whiskey oak, ripe banana, and cocoa. Expect wine-like aromas with a hint of gentle, sweet cardamom and a lingering Irish cream finish in a cup that’s layered and complex. 

Our roasters recommend brewing it black, either as an espresso, cold brew, pour over or using an AeroPress. 

Note: The whiskey tasting notes in this coffee are a result of its unique processing. The offering in this pack is non-alcoholic.

Recommended Resting Period: 10 days

products.title: Excelsa by Mooleh Manay Estate
products.body_html:
Komal and Akshay have been exploring species beyond Arabica and Robusta for years. And Excelsa has long been a part of their playground. This incredible species can resist pests, withstand drought, and survive low rainfall. It's also naturally lower in caffeine. But what makes it equally exciting for specialty drinkers is its unique flavour. With this special lot, the producers show how it develops over a 132-hour fermentation.

Ripe Excelsa cherries were picked from trees that grow over 15m tall. After removing low-density cherries, the remaining cherries were prepared for carbonic maceration. Placed in custom-built tanks, they were allowed to ferment in a CO2-rich environment. To guide the process, the producers added select starter cultures. Saccharomyces cerevisiae, the yeast behind bread, beer, and wine, created fruity complexity. Lactobacillus, the bacterium best known for fermenting curd, developed a creamy mouthfeel. After 84 hours, the lids on the tanks were removed. It set an aerobic phase in motion, which extended fermentation for another 48 hours. Finally, the coffee was dried in polyhouses over 12 days until it reached 12% moisture.

Roasted to a light profile, the result is a unique expression of Excelsa. It opens with the aroma of wild berries, setting up a sip with a medium to high body. Layers of red plum, ripe banana, nutmeg, and sweet cedar unfold next. And rounding off each sip is an aftertaste of malt.

We recommend brewing this coffee black as an espresso, a pour over, or using a French Press.

Recommended Resting Period:  13 days

products.title: Riverdale Estate - Mosto
products.body_html:
Prakashan has always treated coffee as something to keep learning from. His curious, experimentative lens has introduced us to many remarkable coffees over the years. Exploring how one fermentation can influence another, this special lot is no different.  

As coffee cherries ferment, they release a microbe-rich liquid called Mosto. Prakashan and his team collected it from a Gesha they had processed earlier. For this lot, he then used it as a starter culture, guiding SLN 9 cherries through a 72-hour fermentation. Slow drying on raised beds for 25-30 days locked the developments that had set in. The result is a coffee with remarkable complexity and character.  

It brews cups that bring a delicate balance of bright, fruity layers and florality, on the nose and in the sip. A silky mouthfeel unwraps notes of pink pomelo, tart cherries, chamomile, and pomegranate. Adding further depth and delight is the gooseberry-like finish.

products.title: Raxidi Lobo Estate - Pichia Yeast
products.body_html:
Over the last few harvests, producers Richard Jos and Rachel Lobo have focused on the anaerobic natural process. Building on lessons they've learnt, they chose the Pichia yeast for this lot.  

Its journey began with 15 seasoned pickers from the estate's permanent staff harvesting ripe red cherries. After washing with fresh spring water and filtering out low-density floaters, the best of the harvest was moved to stainless steel tanks. There, Pichia yeast guided a 48-hour anaerobic fermentation, followed by slow drying on raised beds for 21 days.  

Roasted to a light profile, the result is an expressive lot that opens with the aroma of strawberry jam, trailed by layers that move from raspberry and plum tart to marigold and red cherry. The pleasant, punchy finish that rounds off each sip reminds us of candied orange peels.  

We recommend brewing this coffee black, either as a pour over or using an AeroPress.

Recommended Resting Period:  13 days

products.title: Sampigehoney Estate
products.body_html:
A regular on our seasonal roster returns. This medium-dark roast, processed using the washed method, brews comforting cups with a chocolatey and nutty flavour profile.

It opens with aromas of honey and raisins, leading to a syrupy mouthfeel and medium-high body. Each sip offers layers of zesty orange marmalade, rich dark chocolate, and sweet raisins, rounded off by a lingering chocolatey finish.

Delicious both black and with milk, this coffee is best brewed as an espresso, in a French Press, or with a Moka Pot.

Recommended Resting Period: 9 Days

products.title: Unakki Estate
products.body_html:
Nestled in the picturesque Joldal Palya of Chikmagalur, Unakki estate stretches across nearly 100 acres of lush green forests. This season, the estate presents a balanced medium roast, crafted to capture the essence of its unique terroir and provide a rich, satisfying coffee experience.

It opens with a sweet, honey-like aroma taking you to the delicious notes of chocolate, brown spices and raisins. With a syrupy mouthfeel and a tea-like finish, expect medium bitterness and acidity in your brew.

The perfect companion to moments of quiet, or pleasantly slow mornings, our roasters recommend brewing it black, either as an espresso, pour over, or using a Moka Pot or an AeroPress.

Recommended Resting Period: 10 days

products.title: M.S. Estate
products.body_html:
We’re excited to bring you the latest harvest from MS Estate, a cherished part of our perennial selection. This washed coffee features S795 and a rare Ethiopian varietal, with MS Estate being the only Indian farm still cultivating the latter since it was first distributed by the Coffee Board in the late 1990s. 

When you first taste this medium roast, you’ll notice its unique depth and complexity. The aroma of dried fruits, with hints of apricots and peaches, sets the stage for each sip. As you continue, savour the combination of a chocolatey essence along with a distinct tea-like finish that lingers on the palate. 

A versatile coffee, it tastes great black as well as with milk. We recommend brewing it as an espresso, a pourover, or using an AeroPress or a Moka Pot.

Recommended Resting Period: 8 Days

products.title: Krishnagiri Estate
products.body_html:
A single origin dark roast, this coffee comes from a Rainforest Alliance-certified farm. The producers used a custom-designed pulper to process this washed lot, minimising water usage.  

In the cup, you'll first notice the aroma of brown spices. The brew, characterised by mellow acidity, a heavy body, and a velvety mouthfeel, reminds of oak, toasted walnuts, and malt. A bittersweet finish lingers between sips.  

We recommend brewing this coffee as an espresso, using a Moka Pot, French Press, or an AeroPress. It is rich enough to enjoy black, and also pairs well with milk.

Recommended Resting Period: 7 Days

products.title: Salawara Estate
products.body_html:
Our newest release comes from the mist-threaded hills of Chikmagalur. Crafted by third-generation producer, Sharan, this anaerobic natural lot brews punchy cups with pleasant sweetness.  

Roasted to a light profile, this coffee feels like a burst of fruit from the first whiff to the last sip. It opens with pineapple and molasses on the nose, before settling into red apple, pear, and almond on the palate. Each sip comes with a well-rounded mouthfeel, a medium body, and a zesty finish. 

Our roasters recommend brewing it black, either as a pour over or using an AeroPress.

Recommended Resting Period: 12 days

products.title: Kerehaklu Estate - Blossom Culture
products.body_html:
With the estate shrouded in fog on a January morning, Pranoy noticed unseasonal blossoms in one of the blocks. There, he had the idea of collecting jarfuls of these blossoms for a starter culture. The goal was to see what happens when Kerehaklu's own microbiome shapes processing. 
 
Aiding a 71-hour anoxic fermentation, the blossom culture interacted with naturally processed cherries to build fruity layers and a distinctive jamminess. To preserve this development, the coffee was dried on raised beds for three weeks. 
 
Roasted to a light profile, the result is a unique expression of provenance. The cup opens with the aroma of ripe berries, followed by notes of strawberry, orange blossom, pomegranate, and sun melon. A delicate floral finish rounds off each sip.

Recommended Resting Period: 12 days

Note: This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

products.title: Attikan Estate
products.body_html:
Attikan Estate’s arabica coffee beans come from the Biligiriranga Hills in Karnataka and make for one of our most popular coffees. Sweet with nutty overtones and balanced acidity, this is the darkest of our standard medium roasts and recommended for espresso lovers. It is a versatile coffee that also works for manual brewing methods such as Moka Pot, South Indian Filter and AeroPress. 

Located to the south of Mysore, the Biligiriranga Hills, or ‘white hills’ are named after the mist that hangs over the region. At 1650 meters, it is amongst the highest coffee growing regions in India and grows Selection 9, Selection 795, Cauvery and Kent varieties of Arabica, along with Silver Oaks, citrus, and fig trees.

Recommended Resting Period: 10 Days

products.title: 13th Birthday Blend
products.body_html:
This celebratory blend brings together natural lots from Stanmore, Orchardale, and Riverdale Estates in Yercaud, along with a washed lot from Unakki Estate in Chikmagalur, which forms the base. Its flavour profile takes us back to the Black Forest cakes many of us celebrated birthdays with during our teen years. 

Opening with the aroma of honey and strawberries, the cup has a medium-high body and a round mouthfeel. You'll notice notes of strawberry, chocolate, cherry, and pear, followed by a lingering finish of chocolate-covered strawberries. 

This blend brews well across a range of methods, including espresso, AeroPress, French Press, Moka Pot, and Pour Over. Equally enjoyable black or with milk, it lends itself to a wide range of recipes.

Recommended Resting Period: 10 Day

products.title: Howdia Estate
products.body_html:
One of our roasters' favourites, Howdia Estate returns for Harvest '26. It reminds us of a floral black tea, and is among the most delicate light roasts on our roster. Processed using the washed method, it brews cups with low bitterness, bright acidity, and a well-rounded mouthfeel. From the first whiff, it's florality comes through, giving way to a bright, tea-like sip with notes of coffee blossoms and orange marmalade, and a black tea-like finish. For a clean, nuanced cup, we recommend brewing this coffee black as a pour over or using an AeroPress.

Recommended Resting Period: 10 days

Note: This coffee pack has limited availability and therefore cannot be included in a subscription plan.

products.title: St. Joseph Estate
products.body_html:
Meet the first coffee from our newest partner farm, run by a community of Jesuit priests whose stewardship of the land spans generations. 

A washed coffee roasted medium-dark, it opens with warm brown spice aromatics. Each sip carries a syrupy mouthfeel and reminds of grapefruit, roasted almond, and toffee. Its medium-high body gives the cup a comforting depth, complemented by a chocolatey aftertaste. 

Our roasters recommend brewing it as an espresso, or using an AeroPress, Moka Pot, or French Press. A versatile brew, it pairs well with milk, and holds its own black.

Recommended Resting Period: 11 Days

products.title: Raxidi Lobo Estate - Anaerobic Natural
products.body_html:
We've been excited to collaborate with Raxidi Lobo Estate since their debut with us last year. So, when we first tasted a sample of this anaerobic natural lot, we knew it had to be a part of Harvest '26.  

To bring it to life, the producers started fermenting some of the season's best cherries. Introducing a specially curated yeast strain to the mix, they let the process go on for 48 hours. Finally, slow drying on raised beds for 21 days locked flavour.  

Roasted to a medium profile, the result is a cup that carries the sweet nostalgia of drinking mosambi juice in summer. It opens with berries and cherry on the nose, then settles into tart-sweet, bright notes of mosambi, green apple, and plum. The mouthfeel is velvety with a medium body, and the finish is long and tea-like.  

Our roasters recommend brewing it black, either as a pour over, or using an AeroPress.

Recommended Resting Period: 11 Days

Note: This coffee pack has limited availability and therefore cannot be included in a subscription plan.

products.title: Kerehaklu Estate
products.body_html:
Harvest '26 debuts with a bright, citrusy light roast. A Kerehaklu special, it shows Pranoy and Ajoy's sure hand with washed processing. 

Ripe red Selection 9 cherries collected by seasoned pickers marked the lot's foundation. The producers then used a starter made from the farm's local microbes to aid fermentation. Monitoring temperature and pH regularly, they finished within 37 hours. Next, the coffee was mechanically washed and dried in the shade for three days. Finally, 12 days of polyhouse drying on raised beds locked its flavour. This controlled, aerobic washed process built complexity while harnessing the bean's inherent character.  

Roasted to a light profile, the coffee delivers clean cups that open with the aroma of orange blossoms and brown sugar. Notes of orange, black tea, and green grapes follow, wrapped in a juicy mouthfeel. Expect low bitterness, medium-high acidity, and a lingering finish of orange marmalade.  

Our roasters recommend brewing it black, either as a pour over, or using an AeroPress.

Recommended Resting Period: 12 Days

Note: This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

products.title: Sandalwood Estate
products.body_html:
A beloved part of our perennial selection, Sandalwood Estate brews cups with tasting notes of rich dark chocolate, sweet prune and zesty orange marmalade. This washed coffee, with coffee beans of the Sarchimor variety, was grown at a lush coffee estate in Coorg. If you’ve tried our coffees from Attikan and Baarbara Estates, you’ll love the chocolatey flavour profile of this medium-dark roast.  

This heavy bodied coffee has a smooth, syrupy mouthfeel which can best be enjoyed when brewed as an espresso or using a Moka Pot or French Press. The long, sweet aftertaste of butter biscuits and dried fruit comes through beautifully when you allow the brew to cool down a little. 

Recommended Resting Period: 11 Days

products.title: Dhak Blend
products.body_html:
Our Dhak Blend is an ode to one of our favourite Indian trees with its colorful flame-like flowers that signal the onset of Spring. The coffees used in this blend are naturally processed which means that the coffee beans are dried with the cherry, resulting in complex, fruity and sweet flavours.

Roasted dark to bring out flavours of dark chocolate and fruit jam, this blend's heavy cocoa body leaves a smooth lingering aftertaste.

Our roasting team recommends the Dhak Blend for espresso-based drinks as well as manual brews such as the Moka Pot and the French Press.

Recommended Resting Period: 9 Days

products.title: Silver Oak Café Blend
products.body_html:
If our baristas have brewed you an espresso-based drink at any of our coffee shops, you’ll be familiar with this special offering since it’s our signature house blend!  

A small way of bringing our cafe experience to you, this blend features a combination of ground coffee beans, processed using either the washed or the unwashed method. This versatile medium roast is named after the Silver Oak trees commonly found across coffee plantations in Southern India. It works well in espresso-based drinks as well as in manual brews such as AeroPress, pour over or in cold brews. 

Recommended Resting Period: 8 Days

products.title: Amaltas Blend
products.body_html:
An ode to the vibrant burst of yellow that marks the beginning of Indian summers, this blend is our go-to choice for crafting a refreshing batch of coffee including cold brews. In fact, this was originally called the Cold Brew Blend Light but owing to its diversity (its flavours shine through in a Pour Over or Aeropress), we decided to rename it after one of our favourite neighbourhood trees. 

A blend of washed and natural processed coffees, we’ve roasted it light to accentuate fruity and refreshing citrus notes. The result? Balanced cups with notes of blueberry and milk chocolate, with each sip concluding with a chocolatey finish.  

This light and fruity favourite is best enjoyed black.

Recommended Resting Period: 16 Days

products.title: Cold Brew Blend Bold
products.body_html:
Roasted to a medium-dark profile, this blend is perfect for brewing refreshing, full-bodied glasses of cold brew. Expect low acidity, notes of dark chocolate, toffee, and roasted nuts, and a bittersweet finish.

Recommended Resting Period: 11 Days

products.title: Baarbara Estate
products.body_html:
Coffee beans from Baarbara Estate, roasted to a medium-dark profile, have a wonderful aroma of sweet caramel and dried apricot. We love this coffee’s intense, chocolatey flavour profile. When roasted medium-dark, the result is a medium-bodied cup that invites with sweet aromas of butter biscuits, treating you to notes of cocoa nibs and dried fruit, concluding with the aftertaste of dark chocolate. Best enjoyed when brewed as an espresso, in the Moka Pot or the French press, the nutty flavour profile of this coffee makes for a delicious cup, either with milk or black.

Rooted in natural farming practices for generations, the farmers use composted fruit and vegetable waste to nourish the soil and neem oil treatments to safeguard against pests. Formed last year, Vishalakshi has helped guide these villages from commercial coffee cultivation towards specialty practices. There is now a growing focus on pruning plants, selective picking, proper storage of beans, and careful processing.  

Roasted to a medium profile, this honey sun-dried lot brews clean, balanced cups. It opens with brown sugar and melon, giving way to roasted almonds, prunes, and a whisper of brown spice. The body is round and syrupy; the finish is long and zesty.

products.title: Riverdale Estate - Gesha Natural
products.body_html:
A decade ago, Prakashan from Riverdale Estate planted Gesha, one of the world’s rarest coffee varietals, on his farm in Yercaud. In 2023, after eight years of care, came Riverdale’s first Gesha harvest—one that we roasted as part of our debut Nano-X lineup. Since then, this rare varietal has become a core part of our Nano-X, a limited-edition series featuring experimental lots, crafted by a handful of producers and creative Blue Tokai roasters. 

This year’s produce, as Prakashan puts it, is the best so far. The plants have matured and come into their own. The processing has become more and more refined over harvests. And thanks to Subham’s seasoned hands, the same goes for our roasting. 

The lot we sourced was processed using the carbonic maceration method. Ripe, high-density cherries were placed in purpose-built drums. Using special valves, the drums were made oxygen-free and CO2 rich. This controlled fermentation pushed the Gesha’s already exceptional character and complexity further. Slow, controlled drying helped lock in these developments. 

Given the high density of the beans and their delicate aromatics, this Gesha was a worthy challenge for Subham. Drawing on both experience and a bit of experimentation, he added airflow during the development phase of roasting by opening the hopper chute. This reduced the heavy caramelisation that usually builds at this stage, creating an air-roaster-like profile and unlocking striking clarity in the cup. 

We’re excited to present the result: an exceptional nano lot that opens with the aroma of sun melon and orange blossom. A bright and silky mouthfeel reveals layered notes of canary melon, cherries, jasmine, and wild berries. Finishing each sip is an aftertaste of cranberries, adding yet another layer of delightful complexity to your experience. 

We recommend this coffee black, brewed as a Pour Over, or using an AeroPress.

Recommended Resting Period: 6 Days

products.body_html:
Our first-ever single-origin, specialty Half-Caff comes from Yelnoorkhan Estate. We selected their S795, washed processed coffee to create a complex and distinctive cup.  

To reduce caffeine by 55%, we used CO₂ decaffeination, a chemical-free, minimal-waste generating method that is conscious in its water and energy usage. We chose it because the other decaffeination methods available to us in India came with a catch. In removing all the caffeine, they also took away the depth that makes a cup memorable. Adding artificial flavours was not something we wanted to do, never mind the fact that many of these methods also used far too much water.  

The result is a cup with a gentler kick that holds its own in terms of flavour. You’ll first notice chocolate biscuits on the nose as well as your palate. A silky mouthfeel then reveals notes of roasted hazelnuts and malt, followed by a long, nutty finish. 

For the best experience, brew this coffee using an espresso machine. It tastes great black and is equally suited to milk-based beverages.

products.title: Riverdale Estate – Fruit Punch

Producer Series ’25 opens with a welcome return from Prakashan Balaraman of Riverdale, a pioneer pushing boundaries through experiments with fruit fermentation and rare varietals. 

For this special lot, Prakashan went a step further, using a blend of tropical fruits during fermentation instead of just one. Ripe cherries were handpicked and triple-washed to remove any floaters before fermentation began. During the first stage, tropical fruits were added in just the right amount to prolong fermentation with natural sugars. Next, in purpose-built tanks, CO₂ was used to flush out oxygen, creating a low-oxygen environment that extended fermentation even further and deepened complexity. After slow drying on raised beds, the coffee was allowed to rest for six weeks for the flavours to stabilise. 

Choosing a light roast profile, our head roaster Shreyas helped shape a cup that opens with the aroma of rich tropical fruits. Bright notes of peach and strawberry follow, layered with hints of red grape and tangerine. A juicy mouthfeel carries through to a clean, lingering mango finish—all coming together to deliver the fruit-forward character that inspired the name, Fruit Punch. 

We recommend brewing this expressive coffee black, as a Pour Over, or using an AeroPress.

products.title: Ratnagiri Estate - YC 01
products.body_html:
Run by Ashok and Divya Patre, Ratnagiri Estate has been steadily advancing specialty processing through their science-led approach. In recent years, they have added a microbiology lab, bioprocessing unit, and climate-controlled drying chamber to the farm. With this special coffee, we offer a window into the innovative work they are doing. 

To process this lot, ripe cherries were placed in bio-reactors after floater removal. In a CO₂ rich environment, two strains of yeast developed using the farm’s own organic matter, together with lactic acid bacteria, drove a 76-hour fermentation. Finally, the coffee was slow-dried on raised beds for 29 days to lock in flavour development. 

Roasted light by Subham from our team, the result is a cup with both floral and fruity layers. A velvety mouthfeel unfolds into notes of jasmine, custard apple, forest honey, and earl grey tea. Concluding each sip is a tea-like finish.  

We recommend brewing this coffee black, as a Pour Over, or using an AeroPress.

products.title: SICC - Excelsa
products.body_html:
Most experimentation with specialty coffee revolves around Arabica. But, at Mooleh Manay Estate, Komal and Akshay are asking what else deserves exploration. Researching alternative coffee species, the two are not only working on climate-proofing specialty coffee but are also pushing the boundaries of flavour.  

This special lot, crafted entirely using beans grown on the Excelsa species, is an example of the same. Since Excelsa is a 20-meter-tall tree, pickers used ladders to harvest the fruit. Ripe cherries were then sorted by submerging in water, removing floaters that are usually underripe or defective. The remaining cherries were then fermented for 84 hours, in a CO2 rich environment, alongside a custom culture. Finally, the cherries were dried inside a polyhouse, with continuous raking to ensure even drying.  

Tyler, head of our roasting department, and Subham, one of our first roasters at Blue Tokai, collaborated to fine-tune this lot's roast profile. The result is an intense cup that opens with the aroma of wild berries, and treats you to notes of cola, black currant, ripe banana, and molasses. And even when paired with milk, this coffee holds its distinctive and punchy profile.  

We suggest brewing it as an espresso, a Pour Over, or a French Press.

Recommended Resting Period: 15 Days

products.title: Garigekhan Estate - CAT - 129
products.body_html:
We’re excited to share our first release from Garigekhan Estate, a special lot in more ways than one. It marks the estate’s foray into a new Arabica varietal, and showcases what close collaboration between roasters and producers can achieve. 

In 2020, Garigekhan introduced Catimor 129, a low-intervention varietal, to their land. The producers planted 170 plants and have spent the past few years observing how the variety has taken to their terroir. Naturally resistant to coffee leaf rust and coffee berry disease, Catimor 129 holds fascinating possibilities, especially when processed with care. And this year marks the first time it has yielded a specialty-grade crop. 

Our Head of Sourcing, Asif, worked closely with the producers to refine the lot’s processing. Learning from last year’s trials, when a shorter fermentation left the mucilage only partially broken down, they experimented with a longer, 120-hour anaerobic ferment. products.title: Warsanlyngdoh Coffee Collective
products.body_html:
It's always exciting for us to partner with a new farm. With Meghalaya's Warsanlyngdoh Coffee Collective, that excitement runs even deeper. A completely new coffee growing region for us, it speaks of the possibilities that the North East Indian soil holds for specialty production. The collective’s origin goes back a decade, when Daman, a first-generation coffee producer, visited Nongryniang—a remote village in Khasi Hills and home to the nanny who cared for him in his early years. 

"There, nestled among the misty hills, I came across two old coffee plants growing in someone’s backyard. I later learned that back in the 1980s, the government had briefly launched a coffee planting program in the area. Like many such initiatives, it had long been abandoned and forgotten. But those plants stayed with me. And so did the people.", he recounts. Since then, Daman started a decade-long pursuit of craft and community. From shading systems to post-harvest processing, he spent years learning all it takes to grow high-quality coffee. Over time, the collective has grown in both, resolve and numbers, with 75 farmers now contributing to a harvest. They pick only the ripest cherries by hand, which are sun-dried for 15–22 days depending on weather conditions.  

The first coffee that we’ve sourced from the collective is a natural lot we’ve chosen to roast to a medium profile. It brews cups that open with the aroma of raisins, unfolding into a creamy mouthfeel. Notes of blueberry, black tea, and khasi mandarin carry through in each sip, with a long, marmalade-like finish. A balanced coffee, it lends well to various brewing methods, including espresso, Moka Pot, French Press, and AeroPress. It is enjoyable on its own as well as in milk-based beverages.

Recommended Resting Period: 13 Days

products.title: Mooleh Manay Estate – CM Natural
products.body_html:
Returning to our Producer Series after 2023, Komal Sable and Akshay Dashrath share their first experiment with carbonic maceration. Building on the clarity and consistency they achieved with anaerobic fermentation last season, the fifth-generation producers modified their drums to create a CO₂-rich, oxygen-free environment that allows for slower, more controlled fermentation within whole cherries. 

The process began by removing floaters to select only ripe, dense cherries, followed by a brief pre-drying phase to reduce surface moisture. The cherries were then sealed in drums, and a custom culture was introduced to extend the fermentation. Over 60 hours, this combination of carbonic maceration and yeast inoculation ensured thorough mucilage breakdown and the development of deep complexity. 

Post-fermentation, the cherries were dried on raised beds inside a polyhouse. Continuous raking over 7 to 10 days ensured even drying until a final moisture level of 11–12% was reached. 

Roasted light by Rishab from our team, this coffee offers a well-structured cup with notes of fermented red fruit and a bright, juicy sweetness. It opens with the aroma of mixed berries and carries a syrupy mouthfeel, with layered flavours of dried fig, plum, black grape, and mulberry. A chocolatey aftertaste marks the finish, adding further depth. 

We recommend brewing this expressive coffee black, as a Pour Over, or using an AeroPress.

Recommended Resting Period: 16 Days

Note: This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in subscription.

products.title: SKIA Coffee (Pack of 2)
products.body_html:
This two-pack (100 gms each) brings together distinct coffees from Nelaji Village in Coorg. Grown by smallholder farmers and processed by Ashish Rao, a first-generation producer, these lots mark our first collaboration with Skia Coffee. 

Ripe, high-density cherries were pulped with the mucilage left intact, then placed in sealed tanks for a 72-hour anaerobic fermentation. A yeast strain purpose-built for controlled fermentation was introduced during this stage to develop complexity. 

From there, the two lots took separate paths. 

Honey Sun Dried  

The first lot was dried slowly on raised beds under controlled shade. Roasted to a medium profile, it makes for a balanced cup with notes of sweet lime, prunes, and almond.

Thermal Shock  

This second lot was immersed in hot water, then rapidly cooled in ice. It was then mechanically washed and dried slowly under shade. Also roasted to a medium profile, it brews cups with notes of tangerine, brown sugar, and berries.  

Both coffees brew beautifully as an espresso or with an AeroPress, Moka Pot, or French Press. They taste great black and pair well with milk. Together, they offer a chance to explore how thoughtful shifts in processing shape flavour in the final cup.  

Recommended Resting Period: 12 Days

products.title: Kerehaklu Estate - Peaberries
products.body_html:
This special two-pack(125 gms each), crafted in partnership with Kerehaklu Estate, features our favourite mutation, a Peaberry. Coffee cherries usually hold two seeds but about 5-10% of the time, just one seed grows inside the cherry. This is a Peaberry. Small, round, and denser than regular coffee beans, it boasts a unique flavour profile, with a deeper sweetness and a brighter acidity. 

Carefully isolated by Pranoy, Ajoy, and team at the farm, the Peaberries that lent to the creation of this pack were processed in two distinct ways: - 

Washed (Aerobic Sequential)  

This lot underwent a sequential aerobic fermentation, where Peaberries were submerged in water for an extended period, creating an oxygen-rich environment that brought out complexity, clarity, and bright acidity.  

Roasted light, these make for a cup with the aroma of brown sugar and citrus, and a juicy mouthfeel that opens into notes of mosambi, toffee, and green grape. The aftertaste is sweet and reminds of ripe mosambis.  

Natural (Anoxic) 

Fermented in an oxygen-free environment, the coffee cherries in this lot experienced a slower, more complex fermentation, since the microbes had more time to break down the sugars present, and produce a wider range of aromatic compounds. The result is a rich, fruity flavour profile with a deep body and balance.  

Roasted light, these make for a cup with the aroma of red grape and dark cherries, and a creamy mouthfeel revealing notes of orange, red grape, and red apple. Punctuating each sip is a lingering aftertaste of red apple.   

We recommend brewing these coffees black as a Pour Over or using an AeroPress.

Recommended Resting Period: 15 Days

products.title: MSP Micro Lot Blend
products.body_html:
A melting pot of micro-climates where some of India’s finest coffee has thrived since 1920, MSP Coffee is a group of seven estates in Yercaud, including the three that lend to this blend. 

From achieving a surprisingly sweet cup after fermenting coffee with a local variety of bitter lemons to seeing the tail end of a 1000-hour ferment, the group exemplifies how curiosity lies at the heart of their work. The micro lots we picked for this blend come from Bison Valley Estate, Stanmore Estate, and Orchardale Estate and bear this very spirit. 

The first lot was washed and fermented with melon extract, with the processing imparting a unique sweetness. The second underwent triple fermentation: first as whole cherries, then after depulping, and finally after washing. This process uniquely combined quick dry fermentation and long anaerobic fermentation with watermelon, developing complexity. The third coffee was processed using the natural method, with cherries dried intact, allowing the fruit to shape its character. 

Roasted medium, the blend has a fruity and punchy flavour profile with notes of cherry, dark chocolate, and wild berry, followed by a rich, lingering aftertaste of chocolate. 

This blend works well black as well as with milk and lends itself nicely to most brewing methods including espresso, Pour Over, Moka Pot, French Press, AeroPress, and Cold Brew.

Recommended Resting Period: 7 Days

For the third destination, we bring you three 75g packs of coffee from Yercaud, a picturesque hill station dotted with streams and valleys, where coffee has been cultivated since 1820.

  • Hidden Falls Estate, a natural light roast with a fruity and punchy flavour profile, and notes of mango, mulberry, and guava.

products.title: Riverdale Estate - White Rose
products.body_html:
Fermented with rose petals, this layered light roast perfectly embodies why Riverdale Estate is a pioneer in experimental processing.  

Only the ripest cherries, hand-picked from the higher-altitude blocks of the farm, where the fruit matures slowly and develops an enhanced sweetness, were used. Once harvested, the cherries underwent a triple wash with natural spring water to remove impurities, followed by a floating process to eliminate underdeveloped beans.  

During fermentation, rose petals were introduced, setting up the stage for complexity in the cup. After fermentation, the cherries were slow-dried on raised beds for up to 30 days, allowing for even drying. Finally, the coffee was hulled at the estate’s dry mill, where any defective beans were eliminated before being sent to our roastery.  

In the cup, you’ll experience bright notes of blood orange, passion fruit, and pomegranate, complemented by a creamy mouthfeel and a lingering sweetness.  

We recommend brewing it black using an AeroPress or as a Pour Over.

products.title: Wine Barrel Aged Coffee
products.body_html:
Meet our three-pack of wine barrel aged coffees, beautifully merging the world of fine wine and specialty coffee.  

Green coffee beans sourced from Baarbara Estate were aged for seven weeks in Fratelli wine barrels that had previously held three of their exceptional wines. The barrels were rotated every 5 days to ensure even infusion, and samples were drawn regularly to track the beans’ flavour development. After ageing, the beans rested for 10-15 days in our warehouses and were then roasted to a medium profile.  

From this process, three distinct, layered, and comforting coffees have emerged. Named after the wines previously stored in the barrels used during processing, the coffees in this selection are:  

  • MS Late Harvest treats you to notes of black cherry, prune, and red wine. 
  • Sette Collection brews cups with notes of red grape, orange, and walnut. 
  • J'Noon White tastes of sparkling wine, stone fruits, and raspberry. 

We recommend brewing this selection black.  

Note: The wine-like tasting notes in these coffees are a result of their unique processing. All offerings in this pack are non-alcoholic.
